cuaba-cuba--linea-clasica.description: Named after a Taíno word for a fast-burning shrub once used to light ceremonial cigars, Cuaba revived the double figurado in 1996 at the Romeo y Julieta factory and makes only that shape. Wrapper and filler come from the Vuelta Abajo, and the larger Distinguidos and Salomón joined the range in 2003. The smoke is woody, led by cedar and honey, warming to incense and salted caramel.

thirds.notes: Cedar and honey open together; other smokes show a contained vegetal note with leather instead.
The honey fades into deeper cedar, warmed by incense and, now and then, a brief cool note.
Intensity builds slightly, with a spicy, balsamic finish and salted caramel at the back of the palate.

cuaba-cuba--coleccion-habanos-en-special.description: Cuaba's special productions favour large double figurados. The 2001 Colección Habanos held the Salomón, then outside the regular range, in 300 numbered book-shaped cases of ten for La Casa del Habano. The 20 Aniversario, shown at the 2016 Habanos Festival, is a 56 x 170 mm double torpedo in a humidor, smoking of maple, cedar and earth with cinnamon and leather.

thirds.notes: In the 20 Aniversario, maple and raw-sugar sweetness sit over earth and cedar, with a woody finish and light pepper on the retrohale.
The maple softens a little as cinnamon rises on the finish, and the smoke turns earthy late in the third.
Earth takes the lead with leather, the maple slips to the background, and a hint of nutmeg marks a smooth finish.
